input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the agreement (Sections 12 and 13 contain no cap language, and there is no "aggregate liability" wording elsewhere). It is mutual and mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, and it carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap at all — direct damages are open-ended for both parties, including for Sparkling. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of twelve months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirmed that Sparkling's fee payment obligations are not capped damages, retaining the existing Section 13/14 carve-out. Note that "fees" is not a defined term but is set by the Fee Schedule (Section 11), so the cap basis is the full licence and maintenance fee stream rather than an illusory set-up fee.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual monetary liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 15
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties' direct liability is open-ended; we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement remain outside the cap, and Sparkling's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages; a straight twelve months' fees cap is our fallback.

ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights; and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this cap. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
